hypothesis: Selling fully cash-secured one-month ATM SPX put options against a Treasury-bill/cash collateral account can harvest the volatility risk premium and may deliver better risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdown than long-only SPY total return without borrowed exposure. The Cboe PUT benchmark provides a clean structural proxy for this economic rule, but because the benchmark omits actual investor implementation costs this trial can establish only index-proxy evidence, not product execution validity.
pass_fail_gates: at least 70% of seven fixed folds have Sharpe >0
external wrapper max gross <=100% and cash >=0
research_basis: Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index methodology/benchmark: T-bill collateral plus short ATM SPX puts, sized so portfolio value is not designed to become negative at rebalance
Cboe published volatility-risk-premium research comparing PUT and PPUT; option-selling strategies are the targeted independent return source
selection_metric: No option-parameter search. Exact official Cboe PUT index only. Compare to matched-window SPY adjusted-close total-return proxy. Absolute historical gates, high-return objective and SPY comparison are separate; even an absolute PASS is capped at validation=WEAK because execution costs inside monthly option rolls are not modeled.
